subject: SAML grace window, IP allowlist cutoff, and service-account escalation playbook
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@enterprisy.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Todd Miller <t.miller@enterprisy.io>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Onboarding schedule + SAML grace window question

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We have two technical questions before our security review next week:

1) The security team asked if Redwood supports a short SAML fallback/grace window (i.e., 48–72 hours) during the DNS change so we can perform a staged cutover without breaking authentication for ~600 users.
2) We also need a recommended IP allowlist cadence and a sample CSV we can drop into our internal firewall team.

Attached is the mutual action plan you shared; we updated a few dates and marked the compliance checkpoint on day +7. Can someone from engineering confirm whether the service-account provisioning flow can be used to automate API tokens for our integration? We want to avoid manual key handoffs.

Appreciate any quick notes — our internal approval cycle is Monday.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Director, IT Operations
Enterprisy Inc.

Attachments: MAP_Enterprisy_MutualActionPlan_v3.xlsx
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@enterprisy.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding schedule + SAML grace window question

Hi Elena —

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of detail we want for the security review. Quick responses below and Ive looped in Marcus and Priyom for the finer config notes.

- SAML grace/fallback: Redwood supports a configurable redirect window via our auth proxy. Typical approach we recommend:
  * Stage A (24–48 hrs): keep existing IdP binding active and mirror new ACS URL in the SP metadata; redirect traffic incrementally by CIDR ranges.
  * Stage B (48–72 hrs): enable strict enforcement but maintain a diagnostic bypass that allows authentication using previous binding for accounts that fail verification for up to 72 hours.
  * Rollback: TTL-based DNS rollback plus immediate SP metadata revert.

- IP allowlist: we will provide a canonical CSV and suggest a rolling whitelist where you add Redwood's egress ranges per region, starting with a 72-hour open window then tightening to exact subnets after day +3.

- Service accounts / API tokens: Priyom, can you confirm whether the recommended provisioning flow is the ephemeral service-account pattern (short-lived tokens via our token broker) or a long-lived scoped key? We prefer ephemeral for better auditability but Enterprisy might need long-lived for scripted migration.

Ive attached a short snippets file for SAML metadata and an IP template; Marcus will validate the exact egress ranges for your us-west region.

Next steps:
- Marcus to list precise CIDRs and the recommended DNS TTL to use during cutover (by EOD tomorrow).
- Priyom to confirm service-account patterns and a migration script example (by Monday).
- Monica to update the MAP with the grace-window language and share final MAP for sign-off.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0210

Attachments: saml-config-snippets.txt, ip-allowlist-template.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@enterprisy.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding schedule + SAML grace window question

Elena / Monica —

Quick engineering check-in: for us-west (primary) the recommended egress CIDRs are: 34.200.128.0/18, 54.213.0.0/16 (these are the subnets our data plane will use). I recommend setting DNS TTL to 300s for the cutover window and preparing a reverse-lookup verification step in your firewall team to ensure no sticky sessions are lost.

For the SAML fallback we can implement the diagnostic bypass as follows:
- SP metadata will include two ACS URLs (primary + fallback).
- New sign-in attempts are routed to the primary; if assertion validation fails we fall back to the prior binding for requests originating from your known egress CIDRs for 72 hours.

Service-account note: Redwood supports issuing ephemeral service-account tokens via our token broker (recommended). We can also create scoped long-lived keys if your migration scripts cannot support rotation. If you choose long-lived keys, we require an IP restriction and a rotation policy in the MAP.

Ive attached a tiny script that automates creating scoped service accounts and pushing them to your secret manager (see example lines 12-28). Priyom, tagging you for review of the rotation policy language.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Principal Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: saml-config-snippets.txt (v2), serviceacct-provision-script.sh
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@enterprisy.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding schedule + SAML grace window question

Elena —

Concrete recommendation from an ops and compliance perspective:

1) Service-account provisioning:
   - Migration window: use ephemeral tokens via our token broker for the initial sync. Ephemeral TTL = 1 hour, refresh via OIDC.
   - For any long-lived keys you request, we will require:
     * Key scope limited to read-only for the first 72 hours, escalate to write with an approval ticket (ONB-4512).
     * IP-restriction to 34.200.128.0/18 and 54.213.0.0/16 for the first month.
     * Rotation cadence 30 days, with immediate revocation capability from the Console.

2) MAP language: I added a short clause (see attached MAP) that documents the SAML fallback behavior, rollback triggers, and acceptance criteria for the security sign-off.

3) Cutover checklist (summary):
   - Pre-cutover: import IP CSV, validate SAML metadata including both ACS endpoints, reduce DNS TTL to 300s.
   - Cutover day: mirror traffic by CIDR ranges, monitor auth failures in realtime (we can provide a dashboard feed).
   - Post-cutover: tighten IP allowlist to explicit subnets and rotate any long-lived keys created during migration.

Ben, can you confirm whether commercial/legal needs to sign the updated MAP for the enforced IP restrictions? If not, we can proceed with the standard onboarding SOW.

Elena, I attached the updated MAP and the IP template. If youre good Ill push the MAP to DocuSign and schedule a short go/no-go touchpoint for Monday 09:00 PT.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Onboarding Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_Enterprisy_MutualActionPlan_v3_updated.xlsx, ip-allowlist-template.csv
